relations.myth: Creation of celestial light at Tiwanaku
relations.note: Viracocha creates the Sun and sets its course.
relations.source: Betanzos, Suma y narración de los Incas

relations.myth: Creation of celestial light at Tiwanaku
relations.note: Viracocha creates the Moon after establishing daylight.

relations.myth: Creation of celestial light at Tiwanaku
relations.note: Viracocha creates and orders the stars at Tiwanaku.
relations.source: Betanzos, Suma y narración de los Incas

relations.note: Molina describes Imaymana as Viracocha's son or emanated agent.
Viracocha sends Imaymana along the mountain or eastern route.
Molina describes Tocapo as Viracocha's second son or emanated agent.

relations.myth: Ordering peoples along the second route
relations.note: Viracocha sends Tocapo along another route to continue ordering creation.
After Taguapaca disobeys, Viracocha has him bound and cast onto water.
relations.source: Betanzos, Suma y narración de los Incas

relations.note: Some writers equate Tunupa with Taguapaca or a Viracocha-like wandering preacher.
relations.source: Santa Cruz Pachacuti and later scholarship

relations.note: Cuniraya secretly impregnates Cahuillaca through a lúcuma fruit.
The child reveals Cuniraya as its father by crawling to him.
Cuniraya sits among the assembled huacas disguised as a despised beggar.
Cuniraya enters Pachacamac's coastal domain and household while pursuing Cahuillaca.
Cuniraya retaliates against absent Urpayhuachac by casting her fish into the sea.
Cuniraya attempts sexual aggression against Urpayhuachac's daughters; one escapes.
Missionaries and Christian Andean authors equate or subordinate Viracocha to the Christian creator.
Viracocha creates a primordial race of giants before making the second humanity.
Viracocha destroys the disobedient giants by flood or petrification.
